column1: # Covers: carmakers and car/motorcycle models, electronics, cameras, audio and musical instruments, games, consoles,
# game studios and franchises, anime studios and character brands, publishers, broadcasters and newspapers,
# telecom, internet services and apps, retail, department stores, convenience stores, restaurant chains, food,
# snacks, drink, beer, whisky and sake, fashion, cosmetics, pharma, banks, insurers, trading houses, industrial,
# chemicals, construction, railways, airlines, hotels, toys, stationery, watches, sporting goods, sports clubs.
# Not here: 7-Eleven (US origin, in US.tsv), Lotte, Lotteria and Piccoma (KR.tsv), Kenzo (founded in Paris), Pokémon GO (Niantic, US), DMG Mori (DE.tsv).
# Hangul: Korean market names where they exist (도요타, 닛산, 유니클로, 무인양품, 닌텐도, 동물의 숲, 역전재판),
# otherwise established Korean media spelling, otherwise 외래어 표기법 (Japanese: ツ=쓰, initial カ/タ=가/다).
# Sources: Wikipedia "List of companies of Japan", Nikkei 225 / TOPIX constituents, Brand Finance Japan,
# Korean company sites (한국닛산, 한국토요타, 캐논코리아, 닌텐도 코리아 titles), 나무위키 for Hangul spellings; own knowledge.
